730840101.text: Are you the Eremites that I, Afratu, commissioned? Please stop here if you are not.

730840102.text: The area ahead is very dangerous. I've already commissioned the Eremites from the Citadel of Regzar to deal with it. Ordinary people should stay back.

730840103.text: As a Mahamata, it would be a dereliction of my duties if anything were to happen to you.

730840105.text: Oh, that's what all the new adventurers say, but overconfidence is dangerous here in the desert.

730840108.text: See that huge machine over there? It is said to be a relic of the legendary Dahri people.

730840110.text: Hmm, perhaps you're more familiar with the name Khaenri'ah? Dahri is an archaic name that's commonly used in the Vahumana Darshan.

730840111.text: Legend has it that the Dah{RUBY#[S]Khaenri'ah}ri Schwanenritter once piloted these huge machines to combat the monsters from the abyss.

730840112.text: Three Ruin Golems survived that brutal war and were sealed by the sages. This is one of them.

730840113.text: It has been lying there silently for centuries, but lately, it suddenly became active and has even attacked nearby people.

730840114.text: It indiscriminately attacks all living things in its vicinity with beam cannons. This is the first time we've seen such dangerous capabilities in these sealed Ruin Golems. There's no way we can leave it unattended.

730840115.text: The Chaos Cores that powered them should have been deactivated long ago, so it's strange that they can still function... even after several hundred years.

730840116.text: Chaos Cores? Ruin Guards have them too, right?

730840117.text: Oh, you know about Ruin Guards? That makes things so much easier to explain. Simply put, a Ruin Golem is a super huge version of a Ruin Guard.

730840118.text: But unlike Ruin Guards, while they do still have an autonomous system, Ruin Golems are mainly operated by people.

730840119.text: That's the strangest part too. The sages have sealed the path into the Ruin Golem using Suda's Flow, so no one should have been able to activate it.

730840120.text: Did someone get inside by other means? Or perhaps it was triggered by an activation device that we have no knowledge about?

730840121.text: The only way to find out is to have a look inside.

730840122.text: True, though I wonder what's going on at the Citadel of Regzar... It's taking so long for the Eremites to arrive.

730840123.text: The Akademiya's seal isn't the problem. The main issue is the huge rock that's blocking the entrance into the Ruin Golem. There's no way I can move it away on my own.

730840124.text: Ooh, we can help with that.

730840125.text: #That is, if you give the Eremites' payment to us. Right, {NICKNAME}?

730840126.text: Are you adventurers? I can't let you take such risks if you're ordinary citizens.

730840127.text: The Ruin Golem's beam cannons are no joke. I don't know how I'd face the Akademiya if I just stood here and watched you put your lives at risk.

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way to enter the robot

730840301.text: Although I'm the Mahamata in charge of this area, I was actually sent here on a temporary assignment because I was on an expedition and happened to be nearby.

730840302.text: Besides, I'm from Vahu{RUBY#[D]Aetiology}mana. My knowledge of the Ruin Golems is limited to the things I read in history books.

730840303.text: But if I can use this opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of ancient Dah{RUBY#[S]Khaenri'ah}ri, it should be very helpful for my subsequent research.

730841701.text: How's the situation? I noticed the Ruin Golem was acting unusually. Was it because you switched its autonomous system off?

730841703.text: Fantastic! The commission is complete then.

730841706.text: Did you discover any clues about why it suddenly became active?

730841707.text: You tell Afratu about your discovery in the Ruin Golem.

730841708.text: Hmm, overgrown vines? Doesn't seem characteristic of the ecology of the desert. I'm not very sure what they are, but it sounds like they might be related to the Ley Lines.

730841709.text: I've received similar reports in the past about Ruin Machines with damaged cores being constantly "revived" due to the Ley Lines.

730841710.text: There may be many links between the Ley Lines and the machines created by the Dahri that we still do not know of.

730841711.text: And the seals of the ancient sages were created with energy from the Ley Lines, so if there's an anomaly in the Ley Lines...

730841712.text: If my deduction is correct, problems will start occurring in all the sealed Ruin Golems.

730841714.text: Unfortunately, the only thing I can do is report it to the Akademiya. I can't deal with something like this on my own.

730841715.text: I originally came here to explore the ruins of the Dahri people. It had taken me quite some while to get approval from the Akademiya, and I even contacted the local chapter to come and get me.

730841716.text: Who would've thought that I'd run into this mess as soon as I stepped out of the city? But I'm in no position to decline a request from the Akademiya...

730841717.text: Now that the issue is resolved, I can finally continue with my fieldwork. I'll leave the rest to whoever else the Akademiya sends.

730841718.text: Please accept your rewards. May we meet again in the desert.

730841705.text: Great, then it should stop attacking nearby people now.

730840217.text: But that big guy didn't attack everyone around it.

730840218.text: Oh, you know about Ruin Golems? Then I suppose that saves me the explanation.
